ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the figure, in $ \triangle ABC$, $ \angle C=90^\circ$, $AC=BC=3$. Points $D$ and $E$ are on sides $AC$ and $AB$ respectively. Folding $ \triangle ADE$ along the line $DE$ makes point $A$ land on side $BC$, denoted as point $F$. If $CF=1$, what is the value of $BE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw $FG\perp AB$ at point G through point F,

$\because$ in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, $AC=BC=3$,

$\therefore AB=\sqrt{AC^2+BC^2}=3\sqrt{2}$, $\tan B=\frac{AC}{BC}=1$,

$\therefore \angle A=\angle B=45^\circ$,

$\therefore \triangle FGB$ is an isosceles right triangle,

$\therefore BG=FG=FB\cdot \sin B=\sqrt{2}$,

Let $BE=x$, then $AE=3\sqrt{2}-x$, $EG=BE-BG=x-\sqrt{2}$,

$\because$ folding triangle $ADE$ along line $DE$, point A lands on the side $BC$, denoted as point F,

$\therefore EA=EF=3\sqrt{2}-x$,

In $\triangle EFG$, $EF^2=EG^2+FG^2$,

i.e., $\left(3\sqrt{2}-x\right)^2=\left(x-\sqrt{2}\right)^2+\left(\sqrt{2}\right)^2$,

solving for $x$, we get $x=\boxed{\frac{7}{4}\sqrt{2}}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a right triangle ABC, C is at the lower left, AC is vertical upward, BC is horizontal to the right, A is at the upper left, and B is at the lower right; D is located on AC, E is located on the hypotenuse AB, F is located on the base BC, and crease DE is drawn, making A fold to F on BC. Reasoning: According to the coordinate method, take C=(0,0), A=(0,3), B=(3,0). Because CF=1 and F is on BC, F=(1,0). The equation of the hypotenuse AB is x+y=3, so let E=(u,3-u). When folding, E is on crease DE, so E remains fixed; A is folded to F, therefore EA=EF. Calculating gives EA^2=(u-0)^2+((3-u)-3)^2=u^2+u^2=2u^2. Also EF^2=(u-1)^2+(3-u)^2. Set EA^2=EF^2, obtaining 2u^2=(u-1)^2+(3-u)^2=2u^2-8u+10, so u=5/4. Thus E=(5/4,7/4). Therefore BE=sqrt((3-5/4)^2+(0-7/4)^2)=sqrt((7/4)^2+(7/4)^2)=7sqrt(2)/4.
